title: Preconvex Games
Oil Revenue Management: Cameroon's Experience
venue: Book chapter in The Oxford Handbook of the Economy of Cameroon
abstract: Cameroon’s growth performance and development outcomes have not hit the level expected from its oil wealth and abundant resources endowments. This chapter first reviews the theory and practice of oil revenue management in the context of developing countries. It then highlights many political economy factors to explain why Cameroon has not harnessed its natural resources, especially oil, for sustained growth and shared prosperity. The chapter underscores that if Cameroon has ever suffered or is suffering from any ‘curse’, it should be referred to as ‘institutional curse’. Most importantly, the chapter asserts that accountability to the people of Cameroon, not donors, is momentous to transparency and good governance.
abstract_zh: 喀麦隆的增长表现和发展成果，并未达到其石油财富和丰富自然资源禀赋所应带来的预期水平。本章首先回顾了发展中国家石油收入管理的理论与实践。随后，本章强调了诸多政治经济因素，以解释喀麦隆为何未能将其自然资源（尤其是石油）用于可持续增长和共享繁荣。本章指出，如果喀麦隆曾经或正在遭受任何“诅咒”，那么应将其称为“制度诅咒”。最重要的是，本章认为，对喀麦隆人民而非捐助方负责，对透明度和良好治理至关重要。

title: Testing the Dynamic Efficiency of Extraction of Non-renewable Resources
venue: Book chapter in The Oxford Handbook of the Economy of Cameroon

title: The Analytics of Natural Resource Management
venue: Book chapter in The Oxford Handbook of the Economy of Cameroon
abstract: This chapter presents the theoretical framework of how society allocates scarce natural resources. We distinguish between the cases of nonrenewable resources and renewable resources. Nonrenewable resources differ from renewable resources because they have a fixed stock of reserves that, once removed, cannot be replaced. Extracting a unit of resource today means that a lower resource stock will be available for future extraction. For both renewable and nonrenewable resources, the economic analysis aims to determine (i) the flow of production over time and (ii) whether and when the resource stock will be depleted. In the case of nonrenewable resources, we present Hotelling’s theory of the mine as well as its extensions. In the case of renewable resources, we examine the derivation of Faustmann’s optimal rotation for even-aged forests. These building blocks will be used in the next chapter to test the dynamic efficiency of Cameroon’s resource management.
abstract_zh: 本章提出了社会如何配置稀缺自然资源的理论框架。我们区分了不可再生资源与可再生资源两种情形。不可再生资源与可再生资源的不同之处在于，前者的储量是固定的，一旦被采出便无法再生。今天开采一单位资源，意味着未来可供开采的资源存量将更少。对于可再生资源和不可再生资源，经济分析均旨在确定：(i) 随时间变化的生产流量；(ii) 资源存量是否会耗尽以及何时耗尽。对于不可再生资源，我们介绍霍特林的矿山理论及其扩展。对于可再生资源，我们考察了同龄林最优轮伐期的Faustmann推导。这些基本模块将在下一章中用于检验喀麦隆资源管理的动态效率。

International Environmental Agreements under Endogenous Uncertainty
abstract: This paper explores the implications of the possibility of a shift in environmental damages on the participation in environmental treaties. Using a two‐period model where the probability of a regime shift increases in the first‐period pollution stock, we examine the issue of coalition formation under both fixed and dynamic membership. Our analysis suggests that endogenous uncertainty may increase participation. We find that full cooperation may be sustained, but only in the presence of endogenous uncertainty. Interestingly, when the shift in the environmental damage is large enough, the model provides a way to solve the “puzzle of small coalitions” found in the literature related to international environmental agreements. We also find that in period 1 (period 2) endogenous uncertainty leads to a lower (higher) pollution stock under dynamic membership as compared to the fixed membership case.
abstract_zh: 本文探讨了环境损害可能发生转变对环境条约参与的影响。我们采用两期模型，其中政权转变的概率随第一期污染存量的增加而提高，并在固定成员与动态成员两种情形下考察联盟形成问题。分析表明，内生不确定性可能提高参与度。我们发现，只有在存在内生不确定性的情况下，才可能维持完全合作。有趣的是，当环境损害的转变足够大时，该模型为解决文献中关于国际环境协定的“小联盟之谜”提供了一种途径。我们还发现，在第一期，内生不确定性导致动态成员情形下的污染存量低于固定成员情形（在第二期则高于后者）。
